summary: Role scope: keep each role to what the docs define
description: The PRD defines three roles: Employee (submits requests, views own balance), Manager (approves or rejects direct reports only) and HR Admin (configures policies, runs audit reports). The build also lets managers and HR Admins request leave and gives HR Admin a team and approvals (default 1 of 2026-10-14, never in the docs). The user proposed keeping to the docs: only Employees request leave; HR Admin has no team and no normal approvals, only the override, the audit, the calendar and (EPIC-8) people management. This removes the hierarchy problem (nobody sits at the top without an approver and nobody decides their own request). NEEDS THE SUPERVISOR'S OK BEFORE ANY TASK STARTS: it removes behaviour that exists and is demoed, and the supervisor's golden rule is to not change required features or the docs roles. No role is added or renamed. Known limitation to state: a manager or HR Admin who needs leave has no way to request it in the system. Staging data is NOT touched without a separate decision: rows cannot be hard-deleted (triggers), so existing requests of Hana, Sam, Marco and Priya stay as history unless soft-deleted by an agreed data migration.

createLeaveRequest and POST /api/leave-requests refuse a manager or hr_admin (FORBIDDEN, clear message). Request Leave and My Balance redirect them to /dashboard and their nav items and the dashboard balance cards are hidden for them (the pending approvals card stays for managers). The assertRole in the route changes from the employee-only gate it already is; the check also moves into the SQL path so a role change cannot slip through. Tests updated where managers or HR were requesters (decide, team, dashboard, balance, query budget).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: a manager or HR Admin cannot create a request through the API or the page and gets a clear message;AC2: Request Leave and My Balance are not offered to them and redirect if opened;AC3: employees are unaffected;AC4: the existing tests are updated and the quality gate passes

summary: HR Admin has no team and no normal approvals
description: POST /api/leave-requests/[id]/decision is manager only (hr_admin removed from the gate and the tests). Team Approvals and My team are manager only: the nav item, the pages and the dashboard pending-approvals count for HR Admin are replaced by the override count (EPIC-6) and the HR calendar (EPIC-7). The HR Admin keeps the dashboard (company-wide calendar), the audit list and the override page. The decision SQL stays scoped by manager_id for managers. Update the nav-by-role tests and the sidebar by role.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: an HR Admin cannot decide a normal request and gets 403;AC2: an HR Admin does not see Team Approvals or My team and is redirected if they open them;AC3: an HR Admin still sees the dashboard, the audit list, the override page and the HR calendar;AC4: a manager's approvals and team views are unchanged

summary: Seed and demo data for the three roles
description: supabase/seed.sql stays idempotent: only Employees get leave balances and demo requests; managers and HR Admins have none (existing rows on an already-seeded database are left alone, nothing is deleted). Keep the team structure the tests rely on (Marco's and Priya's teams, Leo on another team). Add demo requests that exercise the override: one over-balance pending request. A runbook note says what to do on staging (re-run the seed; the old Hana, Sam and Marco requests remain as history; a soft-delete data migration only if the user decides). Update the demo checklist.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: the seed runs twice with no change and creates no balance or request for a manager or HR Admin;AC2: Leo is still on another team and never appears in Marco's queue;AC3: the seed contains an over-balance pending request for the override demo;AC4: the demo checklist matches the three-role model

description: Browser check as Elena (employee), Marco (manager) and Hana (HR Admin) at 1440, 375 and 320 px: what each sees and cannot do, direct URL attempts redirected, API attempts refused; full quality gate; retro with the removed behaviours and the known limitation (a manager needing leave).
